In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this experiment support the notion that general person impressions affect the recall of information in a way that is congruent with the impression, but the effect is more pronounced when the general impression is presented after exposure to the specific incidents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

people are more likely to encode congruent information when they have a general impression of the person and that people are more apt to retrieve incongruent information when they already have a general impression.
the effects of a general person characterization on recall of information are a function of both the nature of the information and the timing of exposure to the characterization.
the effects of a general impression on the recall of specific information depend on the temporal relationship between the impression and the information, and on the nature of the information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of person impressions can be differentially affected by whether the information was encoded prior to or after exposure to person impressions.
people are more likely to remember things that are consistent with their impression of a person, even if they are not explicitly told about that impression.
people are not just influenced by what they see, they are also influenced by what they read.
